chunks: 5257 - And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Abān, from Ismāʿīl ibn al-Faḍl, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the blood of the Magians, the Jews, and the Christians: is there anything upon one who kills them if they deceive the Muslims and openly display hostility and treachery toward them? He said: “No, unless he is one who is habituated to killing them.”

He said: And I asked him about whether a Muslim is killed in retaliation for the people of dhimmah and the People of the Book if he kills them. He said: “No, unless he is accustomed to that, not refraining from killing them; then he is killed while humbled.”

key_terms.دِمَاءِ الْمَجُوسِ: the blood liability of the Magians
key_terms.وَهُوَ صَاغِرٌ: while in a state of humiliation or abasement

ai.seo_question: Is a Muslim subject to execution for killing a dhimmi or a member of the People of the Book in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a fiqh ruling concerning a Muslim who kills non-Muslims from the Magians, Jews, Christians, and the protected People of the Book. It states that qisas is not applied in the ordinary case, but if the Muslim becomes habitually engaged in killing them and persists in doing so, he may then be executed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5257 - Ali ibn Al-Hakam narrated from Aban, from Ismail ibn Al-Fadl, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about the blood of the Magians, Jews, and Christians - whether there is any penalty upon someone who kills them if they deceive the Muslims and openly display hostility and treachery towards them.
Imam (as) replied: "No, unless he is habitual in killing them."
He further said: I asked Imam (as) about a Muslim being killed for killing a person from the People of the Book (Ahl Al-Dhimmah) or from the People of the Scripture.
Imam (as) replied: "No, unless he is accustomed to doing so and does not desist from killing them, then he will be killed and humiliated."
